D.t: Tina Kotek leads by 5.5 in the forecast and wins 83% of simulations. The cushion is about 112,349 votes; a one point swing is about 10,307 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +2.4 and D +13.2. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +0.7. Your best recent poll is DHM Research for The Oregonian at D +1.9; your worst is DHM Research/Oregon Public Broadcasting at R +1.7. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Multnomah, a projected net 236,616 votes; Washington, a projected net 66,159 votes; Lane, a projected net 31,063 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Clackamas, R +2.5, 10.8% of the vote; Deschutes, R +0.8, 5.5% of the vote; Lincoln, D +11.4, 1.3% of the vote; Clatsop, D +2.7, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Tina Kotek runs furthest behind in Umatilla, Klamath, Douglas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.30 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 53 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 51 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Tina Kotek: Immigration voters 14 to 82, Small counties 34 to 61, Midsize counties 38 to 59. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$4.5M cash against $1.9M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 43% of the 963,640 ballots in Oregon so far, against 31% for the other party. That is 3.6 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points away from Tina Kotek. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Money: Raised $11.4M against $14.7M for Tina Kotek.

R.t: Christine Drazan trails by 5.5 and wins 17% of simulations. Closing it takes about 56,174 voters switching sides, or 112,349 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +13.2 and R +2.4. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +0.7. Your best recent poll is DHM Research/Oregon Public Broadcasting at R +1.7; your worst is DHM Research for The Oregonian at D +1.9. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Douglas, a projected net 28,886 votes; Linn, a projected net 24,384 votes; Marion, a projected net 21,649 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Clackamas, R +2.5, 10.8% of the vote; Deschutes, R +0.8, 5.5% of the vote; Lincoln, D +11.4, 1.3% of the vote; Clatsop, D +2.7, 1.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Christine Drazan runs furthest behind in Multnomah, Benton, Lane. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 48 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.30 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 44 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.75 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 46 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Christine Drazan: Corruption voters 26 to 70, Asian and other voters 30 to 67, Large counties 36 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.9M cash against $4.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
